attacks.claim: Lease ownership is keyed on workerID, but the diff never shows how w.id is generated. If it is not unique per process, the locked_by check in Complete cannot tell a stale holder from the current one. This does not affect the single-replica deployment, but it must hold before scale-out.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: definition of w.id; Complete uses "WHERE id = $1 AND locked_by = $2 AND status = 'running'" with w.id as $2

attacks.claim: The claim subquery filters on status and locked_until and orders by created_at, but the migration adds no index covering those columns. At the current ~20k rows this is harmless, but each claim scans the table, and that cost grows with table size.
attacks.evidence: ALTER TABLE thumbnail_jobs ADD COLUMN locked_by text, ADD COLUMN locked_until timestamptz; (no CREATE INDEX)

attacks.claim: The title says the change lets more than one worker run, but the PR body states replica count stays at 1 and scale-out is a separate change. The title overstates what this PR delivers.
attacks.evidence: TITLE: "thumbnailer: lease-based job claiming so more than one worker can run" vs "Replica count stays 1 here; scale-out ... are separate changes."
